title: Internationalization and Localization Extensions
keywords: dates, mathematics, json, and built-in extensions
learning_outcomes: Explain what internationalization and localization extensions contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: the intl extension.

content.intro: Dates, numeric functions, JSON, and extensions convert data between representations. Be deliberate about time zones, encoding errors, precision, required extensions, and failure conditions. In this lesson, focus on the intl extension; then compare it with locale-sensitive number formatting. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use internationalization and localization extensions when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
